title: The Dragon's Roost
signs: Nothing has walked out this far in a long time.
brief: One ledge, one dragon, and nowhere on it he cannot reach you.
scope: The last level on the course, and the whole of it is the final boss fight. There is no platforming here worth the name - a hop in, an arena, a flag - because the level IS the fight and anything else would be in the way of it.
fight_note:
The dragon fights in two phases and the arena has to hold both.

IN THE AIR it is the only thing in the game with no feet on the ground, and three numbers follow from that. See the "dragon" profile and the flying block in features/combat/enemy.gd.

  * It cruises 156 above the deck it took off from. A player on the flat reaches 143 at the top of a jump, so from the floor it cannot be hit at all. Standing there waiting is legitimate and slow.
  * The two floating stones are 96 up. A jump from one reaches 239, well into it. That is the only reason they exist, and why there are two at opposite ends of the arena: the dragon circles, and a single perch you can be cornered on is a trap rather than an answer.
  * It answers a thrown blast by climbing over it, unless the throw was inside its reaction - 168 px cold, 76 once it has seen one and is braced for the next. So the energy strike still beats it, at knife range, and only while it is down. Which is the same lesson the guard taught on the way here, asked again by something that cannot block.

ON ITS FEET it is an ordinary bruiser and the arena needs nothing special for it: it walks in at 150, which is outrunnable like everything else in the cast, claws at 86 and breathes the standing version of the same fire from 125 to 180. Nine seconds up, seven down, with a drawn take-off and landing between them that cannot be interrupted. That phase is why the deck is as long as it is - there has to be somewhere to back off to - and the gap at 720 is the one thing in the level it will not follow you over.

The deck is dead flat on purpose. A flyer measures every altitude it holds from the height it took off at, so a perch standing above or below the ground the fight happens over would put its whole envelope in the wrong place.
ground_note: The same numbers The Fractured Isles and First Steps are cut with, so all three levels are visibly the same coast. features/world/scenery.gd generates every cliff from `solids`, so the art cannot drift off the collision.
solids_note:
The approach ends at 720 and the arena starts at 816 - a 96 px hop, 45% of the jump envelope, and the gentlest crossing on the course. It is there to say the level has started, not to test anything. The two floating stones are the pack's own islands, 96 above the deck against a 107 apex, and they are the only thing in the arena that is not flat.

The arena is three touching blocks of different depths rather than one, which is the only thing this level's geometry does differently. features/world/scenery.gd draws rock edges at the ENDS of a solid, and a boss arena is by nature one long unbroken deck with both ends off screen - as a single 2064-wide block it came out as a flat black band under a grass line, with none of the broken rock the rest of the coast is made of. Three blocks put a torn rock column at each seam, and stopping them 168 to 240 down instead of 1452 puts open sea under the island. Nothing about the surface changes: all three top out at 648, the turf runs over the joins, and from up there it is one rock.
gates_note:
One gate, and the dragon holds it. It perches at 2100, inside the section, so the wall at 2400 stays shut until it is beaten and its body is gone - a boss holds its section through its whole death, which on this level keeps the camera on the arena while it collapses and climbs out - and while it is shut the camera stops with the wall on the right edge of the screen, which is what frames the arena. Nothing blocks going back: retreating over the hop is a real answer to a swoop.

The wall is the dragon's limit too, not just the player's. session.gd fences a flyer into the section it was placed in - see fly_bounds in features/combat/enemy.gd - because a flyer has no floor to run out from under it and backs away from a player who crowds it, so one cornered against a shut gate would otherwise be pushed out through the side of the screen. tests/diag_arena.gd is the measurement: 272 frames of 900 off screen before the fence, none after.
hazards_note: None, for the reason The Fractured Isles gives: spikes kill outright whatever your health is, and this is a health-bar fight from the moment the gate shuts. The sea under the hop is the only thing here that can finish you without the dragon doing it.
enemies_note: Two bosses, side by side, and the gate at 2400 waits on BOTH. They stand a body apart at the centre of the deck — the Dragon Lord at 1620 and the dragon at 1800 — so the fight opens with the pair of them together and the dragon takes off out of the middle of it. The Lord is the bipedal bruiser that held the Isles archway before the dragon took that fight (see the dragon_lord profile in features/combat/enemy.gd): he wakes inside his 460 of aggro and walks in at 52, and on The Dragon's Roost he is turned up to a boss — he is unflinching (no blow of yours staggers or turns him, only footwork beats him), his hits fling you off your feet, and his close-range special is a leap-slam whose landing shocks the ground around where he comes down. The dragon takes off inside its 560 and breathes far more often here than it did alone (special_cooldown 2.5), to keep the air thick with fire over the Lord. Both stand on the deck like any other enemy, so scripts/check_levels.py can measure them, and both hold the gate, so the wall stays shut until the arena is cleared. The two floating stones are still the only way to reach the dragon in the air, and neither the Lord's claw nor his slam-shock can reach a player up on them — 108 px above him, clear of the 96 the shock rises — so they stay the safe perch they were. On the HUD the Lord holds the plate's main green bar and the dragon the red one beneath it: two bosses, two meters. See boss_main/boss_second in game/session.gd and the boss block in ui/hud.gd.
crates_note: Two, at the mouth of the arena. Nobody needs targets to learn on this late - these are cover you can pick up and throw, and the last thing in the level a blast will reliably connect with.
bottles_note: Milk and brew, three bars of five each, stood side by side on the approach rather than inside the arena. Everything the fight needs is picked up before the fight: once the gate shuts there is no topping up.
signs_note: Two, and neither names a key - the same rule the rest of the course keeps. Both sit at y 512, which is where First Steps paints its own: high enough to read against the sky, low enough to clear the two HUD bars. At 442 the second one was drawn straight through the mana bar.
decor_note: [x, y, piece] with the piece's bottom edge at y; a fourth value tilts it. The two rock_mass entries hang from the sky, and both are deliberately OUTSIDE the arena - one over the approach, one over the flag. A hanging mass over the fight would sit in exactly the air the dragon cruises in (492 world), and the boss would spend the whole fight drawn in front of a rock. Art only, never collision.
